status: Infra runbook; User G8 is integrated. Controller verified the real Gateway/User logout and trace chain with Redis and a test-only consumer; actual User Nacos wiring remains a separate gate.
purpose: Reproducible isolated Windows-native local inputs. Substitute each bracketed placeholder with a fresh dedicated value. No process manager, migrations, credentials, keys or business data are generated by this manifest.
invariants: Run each process from its own directory under a fresh ignored run directory; record PID, executable, selected ports, working directory and start time in a no-secret processes.json before proceeding.
Use Python subprocess with argument arrays and externally supplied environment; never persist tokens, passwords, private keys or database content in command arguments or process manifests.

Keep the existing 3306 MySQL and shared VM Redis untouched. Any local MySQL/Redis for this run must be separately provisioned and explicitly authorized, on fresh ports and with isolated test accounts/data.
Nacos server port and its +1000/+1001 gRPC ports, dashboard, Gateway, User, management, Jaeger, Collector and Prometheus ports must be checked for collisions before startup.

Nacos gRPC and Sentinel transport can bind beyond loopback despite advertised IP settings. Use an appropriately isolated host/network or preexisting firewall rules; this runbook does not change firewall settings.
Reserve a fresh Nacos instance exclusively for initialization; no other process or administrator may write to it while the tool runs. The per-port local lock does not control other clients.

defaults.interpretation: Gateway management 19090 and Prometheus 19091 are explicit local run selections, not their unconfigured JAR defaults. Gateway management defaults to the application port when not explicitly separated. User management defaults to loopback 19092.

build.user: Use an explicitly controller-provided User JAR. Its configuration and integration are owned by User; do not read or rewrite its code here.

launchPattern: Use Python subprocess.Popen(argument_list, cwd=owned_directory, env=private_environment, creationflags=CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP on Windows). Keep process handles/PIDs and record only non-secret metadata. Do not interpolate command strings through a shell.

prerequisites.node: Node.js 18 or later with built-in node:http and node:test

nacos.unpack: Verify SHA-256 before extracting into <run>/nacos-runtime; refuse zip paths outside that directory.

prerequisites.observability: deploy/microservices/observability/native-sources.json pins verified native Jaeger, Collector and Prometheus releases.

startup.name: nacos
startup.environment: Supply SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON privately with nacos.core.auth.enabled=true, nacos.core.auth.admin.enabled=true, nacos.core.auth.console.enabled=true, nacos.core.auth.plugin.nacos.token.secret.key, nacos.core.auth.server.identity.key and nacos.core.auth.server.identity.value. Initialize an admin only in this fresh instance, and obtain its short-lived token through the official auth API. Values stay in the child environment or memory.
startup.ready: GET http://127.0.0.1:<nacos-port>/nacos/v3/admin/core/state/readiness must return HTTP 200 and JSON code 0; /state must report version 3.0.3, standalone and auth enabled. Confirm anonymous namespace access returns 401/403, the separate console listener is available, and the owned Java process remains alive after startup. Using -Dserver.port for the server would also override the console port and cause a bind conflict.

bootstrapAuth.boundary: Fresh, exclusive, isolated loopback Nacos 3.0.3 instance only. Generate a new instance-specific administrator password and server auth values in memory or private environment. Never reuse shared credentials.

privateSpringApplicationJson.nacos.core.auth.plugin.nacos.token.secre: <base64 of fresh random secret bytes; supplied privately>

form.password: <fresh administrator password from private environment or memory>

bootstrapAdmin.success: HTTP 200 and JSON code 0; use only on a fresh instance. This response can echo the administrator password; parse in memory and never log, persist, or display the response body.

form.password: <same administrator password from private environment or memory>

login.success: HTTP 200; read nonempty accessToken from the top-level JSON response, not data.accessToken. Keep the entire response and accessToken in memory; never display or persist them.

bootstrapAuth.initializer: Pass the accessToken as NACOS_INIT_ACCESS_TOKEN and the explicit NACOS_INIT_EXCLUSIVE_INSTANCE=confirm only in the child environment. The initializer sends Authorization: Bearer <token> to admin APIs. A plan is offline and needs neither value.
bootstrapAuth.applicationClients: Pass username nacos and the same fresh password through the application-specific NACOS_USERNAME/NACOS_PASSWORD or USER_NACOS_USERNAME/USER_NACOS_PASSWORD environment variables. Do not substitute the admin bearer token for SDK username/password.
bootstrapAuth.handling: Construct a POST body using urllib.parse.urlencode(form).encode(), set Content-Type explicitly, and call urllib.request with data=body. Never put passwords or access tokens in URL/query, argv, saved logs, shell history, or manifests; never print response bodies or request headers. Handle errors without logging sensitive response data.

checks.process: Retain the owned Popen handle and confirm poll() is None after startup and again after the console binds. An early server HTTP response alone can precede a later console bind failure.
checks.server: GET /nacos/v3/admin/core/state/readiness on the chosen server HTTP port: HTTP 200 and JSON code 0. GET /nacos/v3/admin/core/state: data.version=3.0.3, data.startup_mode=standalone, data.server_port equals the chosen port, and data.auth_enabled=true. Check anonymous GET /nacos/v3/admin/core/namespace/check with a fresh non-secret verify namespace returns 401 or 403.
checks.console: Probe a TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:<console-port> while the same owned process is alive. A listening port is liveness only; it does not validate console authentication or operation.
checks.grpc: Probe 127.0.0.1:<nacos-port+1000> for client gRPC and inspect <nacos-port+1001> for server-to-server gRPC. TCP connectivity alone does not prove protocol/auth. Confirm client function with a real authenticated Nacos SDK registration and an authenticated admin instance-list lookup in the exact isolated namespace and group. The G10 SDK registration worked; console and +1001 listener availability were not separately recorded in that run.
checks.collision: Before launch reserve/check server, server+1000, server+1001, console and all application ports; also check the whole host/network as applicable because gRPC may bind beyond loopback. Do not kill processes by name or port.

startup.name: nacos-initialization
startup.ready: Review plan; ensure exclusive Nacos ownership, then append --apply. Only result created or matching read-only no-op indicates success. The explicit confirmation cannot prevent external writers. See nacos/initialization.json for the observed Nacos 3.0.3 concurrent-create limitation and recovery.
startup.userConfig: The fixed knode-user.relay.json must be present in the exact USER_NACOS_CONFIG_GROUP when fixed config is enabled. It contains only sessionEventRelayBatchSize=50; missing/invalid/unavailable config makes User unready. Existing G8 initializations with a different Data ID list or template digest cannot be extended in place; use a new exclusive verify namespace.

startup.name: jaeger
startup.ports: Use fresh loopback ports from native-launch.json; OTLP HTTP is the Collector export destination.
startup.argv: Use every explicit Jaeger argument and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT/OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER in observability/native-launch.json with fresh isolated ports.
startup.ready: Query /api/services on the chosen query HTTP port. An open port is not evidence that a trace was received.

startup.name: otel-collector
startup.ready: GET http://127.0.0.1:<collector-health>/ returns healthy. Also send an authorized synthetic trace and query it in Jaeger; health alone does not prove delivery.

startup.name: prometheus
startup.preparation: Use observability/prometheus.yaml with Gateway management 19090 and User management 19092 for the explicit local selections, or generate a private copy for other ports. User metrics require its delivered integration and explicit enablement where applicable.
startup.ready: GET /-/ready and inspect /api/v1/targets and a relevant time series; scrape target up is distinct from business readiness.

startup.name: sentinel-dashboard
startup.ready: A page or TCP port is only liveness. Authenticate to the Dashboard, verify the registered test machine and read the specific Nacos rules through its native page. Nacos publish success alone does not prove each client loaded the rules.

startup.name: user
startup.ready: The delivered compatibility endpoints are GET /health/live and GET /health/ready on USER_PORT. User management is a separate loopback listener with /actuator/health and /actuator/prometheus. Enabled fixed config must load valid knode-user.relay.json; enabled governanceRules must be UP. Observability export failure alone does not make User unready. Authority health remains unverified until checked separately.
startup.preparation: The User owner must provide a pre-provisioned isolated schema and confirm the supplied JAR has no additional custom automatic migration path before launch. The listed Spring switches disable standard Flyway, Liquibase and SQL initialization only.
startup.wiring: User-side G8 discovery, fixed configuration, governance, observability and event v2 are integrated; actual User Nacos configuration, discovery and governance wiring remains a separate validation gate. Discovery/config/governance/observability each default disabled. USER_NACOS_SERVER_ADDR/USER_NACOS_NAMESPACE/USER_NACOS_GROUP and credentials have documented NACOS_* fallback; USER_NACOS_CONFIG_GROUP falls back to USER_NACOS_GROUP then NACOS_GROUP. When enabled, USER_GOVERNANCE_GROUP must be explicit. USER_OBSERVABILITY_ENVIRONMENT must equal KNODE_AUTH_ENVIRONMENT, USER_OBSERVABILITY_VERSION and USER_OTLP_ENDPOINT are required, and USER_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE defaults 0.1; endpoint requires HTTPS except loopback HTTP. User generic Nacos config import is disabled. Do not put credentials or private material in Nacos.
startup.discoveryAddress: Local loopback-only binding explicitly advertises 127.0.0.1 in Nacos; configure a routable address separately for non-loopback deployments.
startup.externalDependencies: Provide User-owned isolated DB and Redis connection settings, signing/public-key material and service policy externally; consult the delivered User runtime and contracts/user/service-runtime.example.json for the exact names. Do not place credentials or private keys in Nacos.

startup.name: gateway
ports: <gateway-management-port, explicitly selected local value 19090; unconfigured management shares application port>
startup.wiring: Set NACOS_DISCOVERY_NAMESPACE to the same isolated namespace used by USER_NACOS_NAMESPACE and set NACOS_DISCOVERY_GROUP exactly equal to USER_NACOS_GROUP so lb://knode-user queries its registration group. NACOS_DISCOVERY_GROUP defaults to DEFAULT_GROUP and does not inherit NACOS_GROUP. NACOS_GROUP controls Gateway configuration; KNODE_GOV_NACOS_GROUP controls Gateway governance; USER_NACOS_CONFIG_GROUP controls User fixed config; USER_GOVERNANCE_GROUP controls User governance; DASHBOARD_NACOS_GROUP controls Dashboard rules. The initializer writes all selected Data IDs into its one explicit verify group, so for this run set these config/governance groups to that verify group while setting the discovery groups explicitly to matching values. NACOS_CONFIG_IMPORT=optional:nacos:knode-gateway.yaml?group=<verify-group>. Redis TLS defaults true with chain and host verification; explicit false is only for a deliberate isolated plaintext test.
startup.ready: GET /actuator/health/liveness checks liveness; /actuator/health/readiness must return UP with configured auth and any enabled governance healthy. A disabled governance indicator does not prove Nacos rule loading.
startup.discoveryAddress: Local loopback-only binding explicitly advertises 127.0.0.1 in Nacos; configure a routable address separately for non-loopback deployments.

shutdown: Stop owned services in reverse order using their recorded handles. For attached Windows consoles created with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, send CTRL_BREAK_EVENT and wait for exit; use the platform's normal termination signal on Unix. If graceful signaling is unavailable, report that limitation before terminating only the recorded child.
Verify each PID belongs to this run and has exited; never kill by process name or shared port. Retain sanitized results and ownership manifests.

After the owned Nacos process stops, resolve <run>/nacos-runtime to an absolute path and verify it is strictly inside <run> before removing its data. Remove only explicitly owned Prometheus/Jaeger/Collector run directories. To delete a namespace on a retained test server, first verify the exact recorded verify namespace and ownership marker; the initializer performs no deletion.
